dataset.name: NYC Citi Bike System Data
dataset.license_note: Published by Lyft/Citi Bike as open system data for public exploration. This project uses it for non-commercial, educational/portfolio analysis; verify current terms at the source URL before any other use.
dataset.geographic_coverage: New York City Citi Bike system (all stations present in the raw files)

cleaning_steps: Parsed started_at/ended_at timestamps; dropped rows where parsing failed or end <= start.
Computed trip duration in minutes; dropped trips shorter than 1 second or longer than 24 hours.
Dropped rows missing start or end latitude/longitude.

Dropped a small number of trips starting outside Jan 1 - Jun 30, 2026 (a boundary artifact where the raw 'January' export included a few trips from the final minutes of the prior Dec 31), to keep whole calendar months.
Dropped trips at depot/shop/system pseudo-stations (e.g. ids prefixed 'SYS', names containing 'shop'/'warehouse'/'depot') -- not real public docking stations.
Normalized station ids by stripping trailing non-alphanumeric artifacts observed in the raw export.
Derived each station's canonical name (most frequent observed name) and coordinates (mean of observed lat/lng) across all its trips.

aggregation_grains.temporal_cube.json: date x hour x member_casual x rideable_type
aggregation_grains.stations.json: one row per station, whole-period totals
aggregation_grains.station_monthly.json: station x month x direction(start/end) x member_casual
aggregation_grains.route_metrics.json: top 300 origin-destination station pairs by trip volume

anomaly_method.description: Modified z-score (Iglewicz & Hoaglin) of each day's deviation from its own weekday's median trip count across the dataset, so normal weekly patterns aren't flagged as anomalies. Flags statistical outliers in the observed data; does not claim to identify confirmed real-world incidents.

forecast_method.description: Linear trend fit over the trailing window, adjusted by a day-of-week seasonal index computed over the same window. A simple, interpretable baseline -- not a production-grade forecasting model.

known_limitations: Station-level filtering on the Spatial Explorer is month-grain, not day-grain, to keep shipped data small.
Route metrics show only the top origin-destination pairs by volume, not an exhaustive station-to-station matrix.
Trip duration reflects dock-to-dock time and may include pauses, not just active riding time.
Forecasts are a simple statistical baseline and should not be read as precise predictions.
Anomaly flags mark statistical outliers only; they are not verified real-world events.
architecture: Static frontend (React/Vite) reading pre-aggregated JSON produced by an offline Python (Polars) pipeline. No backend, database, or authentication.
